subtopic: MHA vs MQA vs GQA / KV cache footprint
learningObjective: Compare per-token KV-cache footprint of MHA, MQA, and GQA and its effect on decode-time HBM traffic.
stem: A transformer has H query heads and head dim d. Which comparison of per-token KV-cache size and decode-time HBM traffic is correct? (K and V each contribute one head dim per KV head.)

options.text: MHA, MQA, and GQA all use H_kv = H; they only differ in how the QK^T scores are shared across heads at the software level and therefore have identical KV footprint per token. The performance difference is entirely due to different attention kernels.

MHA has H_kv = H, so per-token KV footprint (K+V) is 2*H*d elements per layer; MQA has H_kv = 1 (2*d per layer); GQA has 1 < H_kv < H (2*H_kv*d per layer). Decode-time HBM traffic is dominated by streaming KV each step, so MQA cuts KV bandwidth by a factor of H relative to MHA and GQA sits between MQA and MHA.

MHA has H_kv = 1 (one shared K, V), MQA has H_kv = H, and GQA has H_kv in between. The naming follows 'multi' for the multi-headed K/V design in MHA and 'multi-query' for the multi-headed Q design in MQA.
MQA halves KV cache versus MHA (H_kv = H/2) and GQA halves it again (H_kv = H/4); both are fixed ratios and independent of the number of query heads.

explanation: Per-token KV cache is 2 * H_kv * d elements per layer (one entry each for K and V, per KV head). MHA has H_kv = H (each query head has its own KV). MQA has H_kv = 1 (all query heads share one KV). GQA groups query heads into G groups, H_kv = G with 1 < G < H. Decode is memory-bound on KV cache reads, so KV footprint per token is proportional to KV bandwidth per step. Cutting H_kv from H to 1 (MQA) cuts KV bandwidth per token by H×.

optionExplanations.A: Wrong: MQA/GQA explicitly reduce KV heads, not just re-share scores.
optionExplanations.B: Correct: this is the canonical definition and consequence.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: swaps MHA and MQA definitions.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: fabricates fixed ratios; H_kv is a design choice, not a fixed fraction.

assumptions: Discussion is about the KV cache of a decoder-only transformer at inference; per-token cache excludes Q since Q is not cached.
GQA uses H_kv = G groups; each group of query heads shares one K and one V head.
nonImplications: Does not imply that MQA is always better; MQA typically loses some quality vs MHA (GQA is the common compromise).
Does not imply that per-token KV footprint alone determines wall-clock latency; batch size and paging efficiency also matter.

performanceClaim.scope: Per-token KV cache footprint under MHA / MQA / GQA
